[[Category:Measure theory]]
[[Category:Probability theory]]
'''σ-algebra''' (also written '''sigma-algebra''') on a set $X$ is a collection of [[subset]]s of $X$ satisfying three axioms ensuring closure under countable set operations. 

== Mathematical definition ==

Let $X$ be a [[set]]. A collection $\mathcal{F}(X) \subseteq \mathcal{P}(X)$ is a '''σ-algebra''' on $X$ if:

# $X \in \mathcal{F}(X)$;
# $A \in \mathcal{F}(X) \Rightarrow X \setminus A \in \mathcal{F}(X)$;
# $\forall i \in 1,2,\dots,\infty: A_i \in \mathcal{F}(X) \Rightarrow \bigcup_{i=1}^{\infty} A_n \in \mathcal{F}(X).$

== Properties ==

=== $\varnothing \in \mathcal{F}(X)$ ===

since $\varnothing = X \setminus X$ and $X \in \mathcal{F}(X)$.

=== Closure of $\mathcal{F}(X)$ under countable intersections ===

i.e., 

if $\forall i = 1,2,\dots: A_i \in \mathcal{F}(X)$, then

$$
\bigcap_{i=1}^{\infty} A_i = X \setminus \bigcup_{n=1}^{\infty} (X \setminus A_i) \in \mathcal{F}(X).
$$

=== Closure of $\mathcal{F}(X)$ under set differences ===

i.e.,

if $A, B \in \mathcal{F}(X)$, then $A \setminus B = A \cap (X \setminus B) \in \mathcal{F}(X)$.

== Special cases ==

* '''Trivial σ-algebra''' on $X$: $\{\varnothing, X\}$.
* The '''largest''' σ-algebra on $X$: $\mathcal{P}(X)$ (the [[power set]] of $X$).
